scenario: same frozen real-history backup, baseline package migration/readability check followed by current candidate package cold-path UI switches on separate COW userData clones

baseline.note: The unrelated startup-selected legacy session showed ENOENT for its historical events.jsonl; the two target sessions rendered without this error. Existing same-source baseline latency results remain separately documented in external-performance.md.

uiBodyObservation.method: native CUA accessibility-row selection followed by AX tree snapshot
uiBodyObservation.readinessDefinition: the target row was selected and an assistant/user message container was present without a canonical-content, ledger, or ENOENT error

traceLatencyMs.percentileMethod: nearest rank; ready proxy sums selection-to-page-request, renderer-page-request, failure-reason-hydration, store-commit, render-commit, and next-paint stages

limitations: The candidate clone profile was globally degraded and is not a healthy canonical real-history profile.
The 150-message target had no History events, remained backfilling, and had a blocked ledger; it measures legacy fallback behavior, not prepared canonical-history behavior.

One small-session AX snapshot did not show a message container on the first observation; a later repeat selection did. It is retained as an unconfirmed/not-ready observation, not dropped from the attempt count.
The AX check did not verify a per-session last-message marker or body digest, and trusted DOM click state was not independently captured.
The stage-sum ready figure is a trace-derived proxy, not a matched baseline measurement of last-message DOM readiness.
All page reads were cold-path. Hot-cache, damaged-cache, maintenance-toggle, maintenance-overlap completion/RSS, and full AC-5/AC-6 package matrices remain unmeasured here.

conclusion.result: supports cold legacy fallback responsiveness on the candidate package; the real-history canonical large-session, exact per-switch body correctness, and full AC-7 comparisons remain open
